what_happened: The operator lifted the scope-guard pause on the replay line a second time. The last attempt, job 20261028-065911-m6m5, left a kept candidate (commit afb5db0, 10 files) that passed fmt, clippy and 1546 tests. The resume fix (kbnb) has now landed, so the retry resumes at the verifier with no planner or producer run. The remaining cost is one verifier call. The event lists no unmet criteria, findings or failed checks.
cause: The scope guard sums spend on a line as one number. It does not record why an attempt stopped, and it does not know that a kept candidate has passed every check and needs only the verifier. A line that is nearly finished therefore looks like a runaway line and is paused. Earlier, the first lift was manual. The resume path that would make the remaining cost small and known did not exist until kbnb landed, so the guard could not tell cheap from expensive. Only an operator measuring the cost could lift the pause, and this has now happened twice.
prevention: Make the scope guard record the stop reason for each attempt and the state of the kept candidate. Spend from an environment stop, such as low disk, must not count toward the line's progress-less spend. If a candidate is kept and has passed all checks, the guard should compute the remaining cost as the verifier cap only. It should then lift the pause itself when that cost is within budget. It should write an automatic record of the decision, so no operator has to measure and override.
proposed_request: Change the scope guard so it no longer pauses a line for spend caused by environment stops or for a line that holds a kept candidate that passed all checks. Record each attempt's stop reason (environment, producer failure, planning failure, verifier rejection) and its candidate state. Count only spend from non-environment stops toward the line's progress-less total. When a kept candidate exists, has passed all checks, and resume is available, estimate the remaining cost as the verifier stage cap. Let the line continue automatically if that cost fits the remaining job budget, and write a record of the automatic decision. Acceptance: (1) a test where an attempt stops on low disk after passing all checks does not pause the line; (2) a test where repeated producer failures with no kept candidate still pause the line; (3) a test where a kept candidate is present and the remaining budget is below the verifier cap pauses the line with a message naming the shortfall; (4) the guard's decision record shows the stop reason and the estimated remaining cost.
